extracted.intended_audience: scientists, natural philosophers, and educated readers interested in the physical description of the universe (physical cosmography / physical geography)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing/structuring the 'physical description of the universe' (physical cosmography): how to define its limits, choose methods, integrate observations across disciplines, and present results in a systematic yet lively style. Emphasises what to include/exclude and how to relate partial facts to a unified whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dignified, grave, and animated language
rubrics_metrics.description: “Scientific subjects may be treated of in language at once dignified, grave, and animated.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write so those with limited prior exposure to nature can be invited in and have their perceptive faculties awakened; language should invigorate the mind and make scientific ideas an accessible source of enjoyment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mere 'popular knowledge' compilations
rubrics_metrics.description: “Deviate as widely as possible from the imperfect compilations designated ... by the inappropriate term of 'popular knowledge.'”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not produce an encyclopedic aggregation of prior summaries; avoid repeating old compilations — instead synthesize and generalize to produce instruction commensurate with the subject's importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show unity and connecting links among phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: The physical history of the world must show “the simultaneous action and the connecting links of the forces which pervade the universe.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use partial facts as materials for a vast edifice: combine results from special branches to reveal how organisms and forces form one living active whole rather than isolated facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value and integrate 'purely theoretical' research
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject the error that branches of natural science are unequal and the stigma of researches termed 'purely theoretical.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that apparently isolated or theoretical observations (examples: Galvani, Huygens) can conceal the germ of great discoveries; avoid dismissing abstract work as unimportant for industry or cultivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precisely define limits and scope of the science
rubrics_metrics.description: First consideration: “The precise limits of the physical description of the universe, considered as a distinct science.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly enumerate what belongs to physical cosmography and what does not; set boundaries relative to allied disciplines to avoid confusion of aims and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a general delineation of natural phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: Second consideration: “A brief enumeration of the totality of natural phenomena, presented under the form of a 'general delineation of nature.'”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer a high-level map of phenomena so readers understand the broad territory before delving into particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the influence of the external world on imagination and feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Third consideration: “The influence of the external world on the imagination and feelings ... as a powerful impulse toward the study of natural science.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for how aesthetic and imaginative responses to scenery and exotic plants/vegetation animate scientific description and motivate study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include history of the contemplation of nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Fourth consideration: “The history of the contemplation of nature, or the progressive development of the idea of the Cosmos.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situate current knowledge within the historical and geographical facts that led to discovery of connections among phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish physical cosmography from related sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: “It is with a view of showing the actual character and the independence of the study of physical cosmography... that I will pause ... to consider that portion of the science of the Cosmos which concerns the earth.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify relations to general physics, descriptive natural history, geology, and comparative geography; state what each discipline contributes and where cosmography's distinct aim lies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define the terrestrial portion (physical geography) and its limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Terrestrial physical cosmography (physical geography) treats distribution of magnetism, continental configuration, mountain systems, mean heights, volcanoes in general, rivers' broad features, etc., but does not enter into laws of attraction or detailed electro-magnetic mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include broad, comparative features of orography and hydrography and general causes affecting climate and distribution; exclude detailed mechanism or exhaustive enumerations of individual features (those belong to specialized geography or geology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on general results, not exhaustive particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: “It is only the general results of comparative orography and hydrography that belong to the science whose true limits I am desirous of determining, and not the special enumeration of the greatest elevations... these details falling rather within the domain of geography, properly so called.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize mutual connections and relations over catalogs of isolated facts; use special facts only insofar as they illuminate broader patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use induction: combine and compare observations to discover laws
rubrics_metrics.description: “It is by subjecting isolated observations to the process of thought, and by combining and comparing them, that we are enabled to discover the relations existing in common ... and it is by induction that we are led to comprehend numerical laws.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synthesize field observations, compare regions, and apply inductive reasoning to derive general patterns such as proportional relations among families/species and geographic zones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe distribution of organisms by zones and isothermal bands
rubrics_metrics.description: In the physical history of the globe, organisms are considered according to 'zones of habitation' or 'stations', and to differently inflected 'isothermal bands' rather than by taxonomic gradation alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasise spatial/climatic frameworks (latitude, elevation, isothermal belts) when explaining distribution, rather than treating floras/faunas solely as catalogued taxonomic systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat descriptive botany and zoology as source material, not the primary aim
rubrics_metrics.description: “Botany and zoology ... are the fruitful sources whence we draw the materials necessary to give a solid basis to the study of the mutual relations and connection of phenomena.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use taxonomic and morphological studies as the empirical foundation, but integrate them into broader geographic and physical explanations instead of conflating aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize numerical constancy and the 'law of substitution' in vegetation
rubrics_metrics.description: Vegetation everywhere presents numerically constant relations; in the same climates species lacking in one country are replaced by other species of the same family — a 'law of substitution.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this empirical regularity to explain how floras differ regionally while maintaining proportional relations among families; employ it as a diagnostic tool in comparative geography of plants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin with the sidereal (celestial) portion and treat it independently
rubrics_metrics.description: “The sidereal portion ... should not be made subordinate to the terrestrial. ... the physical history of the world must, therefore, begin with the description of the heavenly bodies.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start exposition with the celestial/geographical sketch of the universe (a ‘map of the world’ in the astronomical sense) because celestial mechanics are simpler and more certain and provide context for terrestrial inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge differing certainties of celestial and terrestrial sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: The sidereal portion is based on pure mathematical astronomy and has greater certainty; the terrestrial portion embraces more complicated phenomena and is less susceptible to rigorous method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt methodology and expectations accordingly: rely on rigorous mathematical treatments for celestial phenomena and on comparative, inductive synthesis for terrestrial phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose precise and appropriate nomenclature
rubrics_metrics.description: “The selection of an inappropriate Greek nomenclature has perhaps been even more prejudicial ... than the injudicious use of binary divisions and the excessive multiplication of groups.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid misleading or ill-fitting terminology, unnecessary binary splits, and over-multiplication of categories; prefer terminology that clarifies limits and relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present phenomena in mutual connection relative to zones and the planet's constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider phenomena in their mutual connection, and in their relations to different zones of our planet, and to its physical constitution generally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always link local or special observations to larger-scale zonal, climatic, and planetary factors; emphasize how continental distribution, elevation, and proximity to sea influence climate and biogeography.

rubrics_metrics.name: At high vantage points use a systematic, animated, and picturesque mode
rubrics_metrics.description: “The higher the point of view, the greater is the necessity for a systematic mode of treating the subject in language at once animated and picturesque.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adopting broad, synthetic perspectives, organize material systematically and use vivid, picturesque language to make large-scale connections comprehensible and engaging.
